findings.highlight: I might die, but he's long dead.
findings.evidenceJa: 死ぬというのなら、あの男はとうに死んでいる。
findings.governingReading: If recognizing death is the criterion, Archer has long been dead; Shirou became as good as dead when he recognized that condition.
findings.explanation: Archer's metaphorical prior death becomes a possibility that Shirou may die now.

findings.highlight: There's no longer any point in feeling gloomy about my own death.
findings.evidenceJa: 自身の死をどうだのと憂いる余裕などない
findings.governingReading: Shirou feels no fear because his recognition of Archer's condition leaves him no余裕—no room or capacity—to concern himself with his own death.
findings.explanation: No mental room to worry about death becomes a judgment that such gloom has no point.

findings.highlight: I kept my promise to you. I haven't harmed her.
findings.evidenceJa: おまえとの約束は守っている。オレは手出しはせん。
findings.governingReading: Lancer says he is keeping the agreement: he himself will not lay a hand on Rin, whatever others do.
findings.explanation: Lancer's continuing promise not to intervene becomes a report that he has not harmed Rin so far.

findings.evidenceJa: あいよ、と気軽に声を返す。
findings.governingReading: He answers lightly with あいよ; only after that does he stop and turn rather than depart.
findings.explanation: Lancer's casual verbal reply becomes his departure.

findings.highlight: I did act according to my ideals and always did what was right.
findings.evidenceJa: 確かにオレは理想通りの正義の味方とやらになったさ。
findings.governingReading: Archer grants that he became the ideal's 正義の味方, then says the end yielded only regret and death.
findings.explanation: Becoming a so-called hero of justice becomes always doing what was right.

findings.highlight: scattering innocent lives like so much dust
findings.evidenceJa: 無関係な人間の命なぞどうでもよくなるくらい殺して
findings.governingReading: He says he killed so much that the lives of uninvolved people no longer mattered to him, a statement about progressive moral desensitization.
findings.explanation: Archer's erosion until unrelated lives ceased to matter becomes a decorative image of scattering innocent lives.

findings.highlight: Shirou Emiya was clinging to a mere feel-good idealism.
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮士郎という男が抱いていたものは、都合のいい理想論だった
findings.governingReading: Archer condemns Shirou's doctrine as 都合のいい: an ideal theory convenient to the person holding it because it ignores its structural cost.
findings.explanation: A convenient or self-serving ideal theory becomes feel-good idealism.

findings.highlight: A hero of justice can only save the people he's decided to save.
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方が助けられるのは、味方をした人間だけ。
findings.governingReading: A hero of justice can save only the people whose side he takes; the claim concerns partiality created by siding with one party.
findings.explanation: People whose side the hero took become people he had already decided to save.

findings.highlight: Saving as many people as you can with the minimum sacrifice is the right choice.
findings.evidenceJa: 一つを犠牲にして、より多くのモノを助け出す事こそが正しい
findings.governingReading: The doctrine declares it right to sacrifice one thing/person in order to rescue a greater number.
findings.explanation: Sacrificing one to save more becomes making the minimum sacrifice.

findings.highlight: I agreed to a fate of nothingness, to give up my soul to the Guardians and be removed from the time axis.
findings.evidenceJa: 死後、己が存在を守護者に預けたモノは輪廻の枠から外れ、無と同意になるのだと
findings.governingReading: Anything that entrusts its posthumous existence as a Guardian is removed from the frame of reincarnation and becomes equivalent to nothing.
findings.explanation: The general posthumous fate of Guardians becomes Archer's personal agreement to surrender his soul to them and leave the time axis.

findings.highlight: an existence that erases the despair other humans make.
findings.evidenceJa: 人間が生み出した欲望を消す為だけの存在。
findings.governingReading: Archer's endpoint is an existence used only to erase the 欲望—desires or avarice—produced by humanity.

findings.highlight: Whenever they see humans do something that causes their own destruction, they show up and burn it all.
findings.evidenceJa: 自らの手で滅びようとする人間の業を目の当たりにし、それを、ゴミのように焼き払ってきた。
findings.governingReading: The continuing subject is the singular man: again and again, he saw human self-destruction and burned it away like trash with his own hands.
findings.explanation: Archer personally witnessing and incinerating human karma becomes an action by Guardians as a group.

findings.highlight: Hatred at his past self, for valuing the humans who just kept taking from each other.
findings.evidenceJa: 奪い合いを繰り返す人間と、それを尊いと思っていた、かつての自分そのものを。
findings.governingReading: His hatred has two objects: people who repeatedly take from each other and his former self who valued them.
findings.explanation: English confines his hatred to his former self. Japanese also explicitly directs it at the people whose repeated predation disillusioned him.

findings.highlight: However, ever since he died, he can't erase the original Emiya that exists in a place outside of the time axis.
findings.evidenceJa: ヤツは死んだところで輪の外にある“座”に在るエミヤ本体は消え去らない。
findings.governingReading: Even if this summoned Archer dies, the original Emiya in the Throne outside the cycle will not disappear.
findings.explanation: A hypothetical death that cannot erase the original becomes the temporal claim that he has been unable to erase it ever since dying.

findings.highlight: I'm not about to have any sudden hope for a saving grace.
findings.evidenceJa: いまさら結果など求めていない。
findings.governingReading: After waiting for this moment through his service, Archer says that at this late stage he seeks no result; what follows is merely displaced anger.
findings.explanation: Archer's explicit abandonment of results becomes a denial that he expects saving grace.

findings.highlight: you never should have tried to be a hero of justice.
findings.evidenceJa: おまえは、正義の味方になぞなるべきではなかった
findings.governingReading: Archer corrects 'I' to 'you' and condemns becoming that role, whose completed outcome he has just described.
findings.explanation: Archer says Shirou should never have become a hero of justice; English says he should never have tried.

findings.highlight: It probably is mostly pride, like he said.
findings.evidenceJa: それはやせ我慢の連続でひどく歪だったろう。
findings.governingReading: Shirou concedes that his path has likely been a continuous performance of painful endurance and was badly warped.
findings.explanation: A life of repeated strained self-denial and severe distortion becomes mostly pride.

findings.highlight: Shirou Emiya won't back down, not even for what he's lost.
findings.evidenceJa: その、落としてきた物の為にも、衛宮士郎は退けない。
findings.governingReading: Precisely because he lost more than he gained, he cannot retreat, including for the sake of the things left behind along the way.
findings.explanation: Shirou refusing to retreat for the sake of what he lost becomes refusing despite what he lost.

findings.highlight: We're going to go at it bare-handed.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺とヤツは徒手空拳のまま対峙する。
findings.governingReading: They confront one another with no weapons presently in hand; the next line immediately says both are beings who create swords.
findings.explanation: Facing one another empty-handed becomes an announced bare-handed fight.
